name: Halfaya-Kahla Gas Pipeline

values.OtherEnglishNames: Halfaya-Al Kahla dry gas pipeline; Halfaya field associated-gas outlet line
values.Owner: PetroChina Halfaya [37.5%]; TotalEnergies EP Iraq [18.75%]; Petronas Carigali Iraq [18.75%]; Missan Oil Company [25%]
values.Parent: China National Petroleum Corporation [37.5%]; TotalEnergies SE [18.75%]; Petroliam Nasional Berhad [18.75%]; Iraq [25%]
values.RouteNotes: No official GIS route located. Short ~21 km field-outlet line from the Halfaya oil field gas collection/receiving station to the Al-Kahla power station in Maysan governorate, southern Iraq; built by China Petroleum Pipeline Company. Route not staged (geometry belongs in the routes repo, not media refs).

researcher_notes: NEW ROW. Confirmed distinct from the two existing Halfaya-area gas rows: P6832 (Bazargan-Halfaya, 18in, INBOUND sour gas from the Iran-border Buzurgan complex into Halfaya) and P4058 (Eastern Iraq Gas Pipeline, 48in / 350 capacity) — neither matches this 24in / 21km OUTBOUND dry-gas outlet, and endpoints/diameter rule out corridor overlap with P4058. Add-threshold met on all three legs: (a) sponsor = PetroChina Halfaya operating consortium (field operator; built by China Petroleum Pipeline Company / CPECC, a CNPC subsidiary); (b) endpoints = Halfaya oil field -> Al-Kahla power station, Maysan governorate; (c) concrete step = operating (commissioned early 2013). EXISTENCE + STATUS = high confidence (independent: Iraq Oil Report 2013 EN, Zawya 2023 EN, Al Jazeera 2024 AR, NS Energy/TotalEnergies for the operator consortium). SPEC (24in diameter, 21km length, 40 MMcf/d initial pilot flow) rests primarily on the Iraq Oil Report Feb-2013 report, a reputable specialist source, but is effectively single-sourced for the exact figures -> overall tier MEDIUM. Capacity left BLANK: the only figure available is the 40 MMcf/d 2013 pilot flow, which is a throughput at start-up, not a stated design capacity, and is now outdated (the 300 MMscf/d Halfaya GPP came online 2023-2024). Owner/Parent reflect the Halfaya field service-contract consortium (PetroChina Halfaya 37.5% operator; TotalEnergies 18.75%; Petronas Carigali 18.75%; Missan Oil Company 25%) per NS Energy / TotalEnergies; note the asset is legally state-owned under Iraq's technical service contract, and Missan Oil Company operates the processing complexes (Arabic sources, June 2026). EndLocation set to Al-Kahla power station (the documented terminus of this 24in line); the Halfaya GPP's dry gas also feeds the Amara and Maysan power plants (Zawya/Al Jazeera 2023-2024), but that later delivery may run on additional/separate lines and is NOT conflated into this row's spec. mubasher.info Arabic article on the Kahla gas-connection line opening exists but repeatedly timed out in url_verifier, so it was NOT cited. No fabricated URLs; all cited URLs passed url_verifier. Route: no official GIS geometry located; not staged (geometry -> routes repo).
